questions.text: Does the PDE have any interface that allows interaction?

options.label: No
options.finalMessage: The PDE likely falls outside CRA scope. Document the justification in technical documentation. End of survey.

questions.text:
Does the PDE implement authentication on ALL interfaces identified in Question 1?
For each interface: is there a mechanism that verifies the identity of the entity (user, device, service) before granting access? Include both human-facing and machine-to-machine interfaces.

options.label: Some interfaces have auth, some don't

questions.text: Does the PDE ship with hardcoded or shared default credentials?

options.label: Yes
options.finalMessage:
⛔ NON-COMPLIANCE

Violates: 2(b) secure defaults, 2(d) access control, 2(e) credential confidentiality, 2(i) impact on other devices (if credentials shared across).

**TODO**: Implement unique per-device credentials (factory-provisioned or forced first-use setup).

questions.text: Is the absence of authentication documented with a risk justification?

options.label: Yes, justification exists
options.finalMessage:
ℹ JUSTIFIED ABSENCE - VERIFY

Review the justification. It is typically only defensible if the PDE has no network connectivity AND processes no data affecting security/safety/privacy.

Apply **Control Set C**. End of survey.

options.label: No, justification missing
options.finalMessage:
⚠️ NON-COMPLIANCE

The manufacturer must either: (a) implement authentication, or (b) produce a defensible Art. 13(4) justification. In practice, (a) is almost always required for any connected PDE.

Apply **Control Set C**. End of survey.

questions.text:
Where does authentication and access control happen?
Consider the full flow: where credentials are verified, where access decisions are made, and where they are enforced.

options.label: Delegated to customer infrastructure (LDAP, AD, RADIUS, SAML/OIDC)

questions.text:
Was the remote IAM service designed by or on behalf of the PDE manufacturer?
(CRA Art. 3(2): "remote data processing solution" = software designed by or on behalf of the manufacturer, without which the PDE cannot perform one of its functions.)

options.label: Yes, manufacturer's own cloud backend or commissioned development
No, third-party service (Auth0, Cognito, Azure AD B2C, Firebase Auth, etc.)
Partial, manufacturer's layer on top of third-party IdP

questions.text:
What does the IAM function protect? (select all that apply)
The highest applicable category sets the risk level for access control (Annex I, 2(d)).

options.label: Configuration and management only (device settings, firmware update, diagnostic access)
User data access (personal data, usage data, stored content)
Physical safety functions (door locks, medical devices, industrial actuators, vehicle controls)
Access to other connected systems (gateways, ICS, network infrastructure)
Unique per-device (factory-provisioned or mandatory first-use setup)
Shared default, change enforced (device refuses to operate until changed)

questions.text: Does the PDE support multiple user roles or privilege levels? (e.g., admin vs user, operator vs engineer, read-only vs read-write)
Does the PDE store credentials locally? (passwords, tokens, certificates, keys, on the device itself)
Can the PDE operate its essential functions if the remote IAM is unavailable? (Only for remote or hybrid architectures)
Does the PDE log authentication and access events? (successful/failed logins, access decisions, credential or config changes)
Can the IAM component be updated independently of the full firmware/software?
Thank you for completing the survey.
